draft.title: Prices direct resources
card: Resources are what businesses use to make products, such as workers, land, machinery and materials.
When the price of a product rises, making it becomes more profitable. A business can earn more from each item it sells.
Businesses then tend to move resources into making more of that product. They may hire more workers or use more land for it.
In this way, prices act as signals. They guide resources towards the products that buyers are willing to pay more for.
draft.remember: A higher price signals higher profit, so resources move towards that product.

a.q: Why do businesses move resources into making a product whose price has risen?
opts: Making it has become more profitable
Making it has become cheaper to do
Buyers have been told to buy less of it
Other products have stopped being made
a.why: A higher price means more income per item, so profit is greater. The cost of making the product has not necessarily changed.
a.clue: Think about what a higher price means for profit.

b.q: The price of macadamia nuts rises sharply. A farmer near Bundaberg has land growing sugar cane. What is the farmer likely to do?
opts: Use some land to grow more macadamias
Plant more sugar cane on the same land
Leave the land unused to wait for prices
Sell the land to a sugar cane mill
b.why: The higher price makes macadamias more profitable, so the farmer may move land towards them. Planting more sugar cane would ignore the price signal.
b.clue: Where would the land earn the most now?

a.best: Making it has become more profitable

b.best: Use some land to grow more macadamias

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about what a higher price means for profit' points straight at the only option that mentions profit, so a student can pick the answer without understanding the idea.
